title: Enchiladas

ingredients.name: tomatillos, husks and stems removed, rinsed well and dried
poblano chiles, stemmed, halved, and seeded
ingredients.notes: or mix of poblano, anaheim, and jalapeno

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.notes: 1–2½ tsp; start with 1 tsp and adjust

ingredients.name: pepper Jack or Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
ingredients.notes: 2 cups; may need a bit more with the extra chicken

steps.text: Heat 2 teaspoons oil in medium saucepan over medium heat until shimmering. Add onion and cook, stirring often, until softened and lightly browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in cumin and two-thirds of garlic and cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Decrease heat to low and stir in broth. Add chicken, cover, and simmer until it registers 160 degrees, 15 to 20 minutes, flipping chicken halfway through cooking. Transfer chicken to large bowl; place in refrigerator to cool, about 20 minutes. Measure out ¼ cup broth and set aside. Strain out onions and set aside.

Adjust 1 oven rack to middle position and second rack 6 inches from broiler element; heat broiler. Toss tomatillos, tomatoes, and poblanos (or other peppers) with remaining 2 teaspoons oil. Arrange tomatillos and tomatoes cut side down and peppers skin side up on baking sheet. Broil on upper rack until vegetables blacken and start to soften, 5 to 10 minutes, rotating sheet halfway through broiling.
Remove tomatillos and poblanos from oven, let cool slightly, then remove skins from poblanos (leave tomatillo skins intact). Decrease oven temperature to 450 degrees.

Transfer vegetables, along with any accumulated juices, to food processor. Add 1 teaspoon sugar, 1 teaspoon salt, remaining garlic, reserved cooking liquid, 1/2 cup reserved onions, and chiles in adobo to food processor and pulse until sauce is somewhat chunky, about 8 pulses, or also good processed until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste, and adjust tartness by stirring in remaining sugar, ½ teaspoon at a time; set aside.
When chicken is cool, use 2 forks to shred into bite-size pieces. Combine chicken with cilantro, 1½ cups pepper Jack, and black beans; season with salt to taste.

Spread ¾ cup tomatillo sauce evenly over bottom of 13 by 9-inch baking dish. Warm tortillas if using corn. Place tortillas on counter and spread ⅓ cup chicken filling down center of each tortilla. Roll each tortilla tightly and place in baking dish, seam side down. Pour remaining tomatillo sauce over top of enchiladas and spread into even layer so that it coats top of each tortilla. Sprinkle with remaining ½ cup pepper Jack and cover tightly with foil.
Bake enchiladas on lower rack until heated through and cheese is melted, 15 to 20 minutes. Uncover, bake another 5 minutes to brown cheese.  Serve immediately, adding toppings to each plate.

attribution.name: America's Test Kitchen with many edits by Jessica Badgeley

notes:
Serves 4 to 6. About 1½ hours total: poach the chicken while you broil the vegetables, make the sauce, and grate the cheese, then shred, assemble, and bake 15–20 minutes.

Halve large tomatillos and tomatoes (more than 2 inches in diameter) and place them skin side up for broiling in step 2 to ensure even cooking and charring. To increase the spiciness of the sauce, reserve some of the chiles' ribs and seeds and add them to the food processor in step 4. Be sure to cool the chicken filling before filling the tortillas; a hot filling will make the enchiladas soggy.
